target_customer: Residential general contractors and remodelers, plus the subcontractors, retailers and homeowners they transact with
problem: Contractors estimate jobs with outdated manual processes and lack digital tools, so quotes are slow and customers cannot interactively choose materials and upgrades.
business_model: Software subscription plus marketplace take on construction purchasing (reported annualized GMV of $72M in 2021)
product_category: Construction estimating, management software and procurement marketplace

founders.name: Mike Bignold
prior_employers: Own residential contracting company (sold in 2017, per TechCrunch)
founders.background_notes: Built the estimating app while running his contracting company and did some coding in college (TechCrunch, 2021-10).

founders.name: David Vass
founders.background_notes: Named by TechCrunch as co-founder; helped Bignold's contracting business rank at the top of Google. No further background given.

investors: angels including Willy Schlacks, Ryan Sutton-Gee, Jonathan Wasserstrum, Bill Smith

competitors.name: Buildertrend (with CoConstruct)
competitors.what: Cloud construction management software for residential builders and remodelers
competitors.traction_then: Market leader after acquiring CoConstruct in February 2021
competitors.funding_then: Growth investment from Bain Capital Tech Opportunities and HGGC to fund the acquisition

technical_complexity.rationale: A catalog of over 114,000 real items, pricing data and an interactive estimate to point of sale flow is standard SaaS engineering with a hard data curation component.

defensibility.rationale: The item and pricing database and contractor workflow lock in some users, but estimating software is copyable and incumbents like Buildertrend were adding features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy of the marketplace wedge was found in searches; the company remained independent and active with no later round found.

market_need_then: The company says contractors were frustrated with outdated estimating processes. TechCrunch reported $72M annualized GMV and growth of 2,203% year over year from a small base in October 2021.

branding.domain_note: Uses bolsterbuilt.com rather than an exact bolster.com; legal name Bolster Built Inc.

identity.logo: Registered trademark logo (details not described in sources)
identity.voice_and_tone: Positions itself as a challenger in construction management software with the mission of making building as enjoyable as buying and selling online.

rebrands.why: No source states the reason or exact date; the company was CostCertified at the October 2021 funding announcement and the YC page links the two.

brand_strength.rationale: Sources show only trade press and review listings; no evidence of community or virality. The name is a common word shared by unrelated companies such as Bolster Academy.

outcome_analysis: Bolster, formerly CostCertified, grew out of its founder's own contracting experience and reached reported $72M annualized GMV by October 2021 when it raised an $8.45M seed led by FUSE, a record for Alberta per the company. The founder's domain knowledge and fast growth from a small base were the main strengths. No later round, exit or shutdown was found, so the long term outcome is unknown and its status is Active.
notes: Founded year conflicts: YC page says 2015, TechCrunch says co-founded 2017, aggregators say 2015 or 2016. Aggregators (CB Insights, Employbl) list $8.58M total raised; only the $8.45M seed is recorded as a round. Some aggregators credit Y Combinator as lead; TechCrunch says FUSE led. An Alberta record claim comes from the company site. Houzz Pro and Procore are plausible rivals but were not recorded because no source dated near the batch was found.
